label: Information handoff
title: How can people distinguish verified facts, reports, requests, and confirmations when sharing information?
summary: A simple way to keep source, verification status, and confirmation state separate when information is passed between people or locations.
meta_description: Ready.gov and FEMA guidance adapted into a low-risk checklist for distinguishing verified information, reports, requests, and confirmations.
lead: Information can change as it passes through several people. Keeping content separate from its verification or confirmation state helps reduce confusion.
scope: Low-risk preparedness communication and information handoff
basis: Ready.gov communication planning + FEMA NIMS information verification + verified S03 PUBLIC_ARCHIVE
footer: This is general information-management guidance. Follow current official instructions during an actual disaster and use qualified authorities for professional safety judgments.

blocks.text: FEMA NIMS training emphasizes gathering information, verifying accuracy, coordinating for consistency, and then disseminating accurate and timely information. A small group can adapt that principle by marking whether an item is a report, verified fact, request, confirmation, or still unknown.

rows: Received from another person but not independently confirmed
Confirmed directly or with a responsible source
Asked for, but not yet accepted or confirmed
Accepted with a defined scope or condition
Important information that is still unresolved

blocks.text: These status names are an editorial adaptation, not an official FEMA classification table.

sections.heading: Keep source and time with the information

items: What needs to be checked again

sections.heading: Keep an offline copy when networks may be unreliable

blocks.text: Ready.gov communication-planning guidance recommends preparing contact information in advance and keeping paper copies because normal communication networks may be unreliable.

The verified SESSION_003 Archive distinguishes an introduction from a confirmed reservation and keeps second-hand information labeled as unverified. That scene prompted the general question of how to preserve information status during handoff.
